records.name_note: Admissible sources split on the primary common name. NC State's Common Name(s) list for Salvia coccinea is alphabetized and reads Bloody Sage, Indian Fire, Red Sage, Scarlet Sage, matching the page-title parenthetical order; it does not list Tropical Sage. UF/IFAS's dedicated page is titled "Scarlet Salvia, Scarlet Sage", and its common-name line lists scarlet salvia, scarlet sage, tropical sage, blood sage. Bloody Sage was chosen as the first item of NC State's list; Tropical Sage and Blood Sage appear only in UF/IFAS's list, not as its first item. NC State's description prose opens with 'Scarlet sage'; this catalog already lands Scarlet Sage as the common name of Salvia splendens, so that name is not used here.
records.toxicity_detail: NC State's tag list for Salvia coccinea carries three separate tags, "#non-toxic for cats", "#non-toxic for horses" and "#non-toxic for dogs"; the page has no Poison block and no Problems field. No other admissible source consulted states toxicity for this taxon.
unknowns: Missouri Botanical Garden: the only Plant Finder page found for this species name is the cultivar page for Salvia coccinea 'Forest Fire', which is cultivar-only and also could not be fetched here, so no MoBot content was used. No dedicated RHS page for Salvia coccinea was found. Clemson HGIC has only a genus-level Salvia page, so it was not used.

toxic_to_pets=false rests solely on NC State's '#non-toxic for cats' and '#non-toxic for dogs' tags; no Poison block or symptom list exists on that page, and no other admissible source addresses toxicity.

water_regime left null: NC State says it 'tolerates drought but will flower more abundantly with watering during dry spells' and UF/IFAS says 'very drought tolerant' (both tolerance traits, not a watering instruction); UF/IFAS's 'moist, well-drained soil' is a soil description. No source gives a watering cadence, so the day-interval and dry-down fields are null.
soil_ph_min and soil_ph_max left null: NC State lists Acid (<6.0), Neutral (6.0-8.0) and Alkaline (>8.0), which are open-ended bands, and UF/IFAS lists acidic and alkaline tolerance.
Size sources disagree: NC State gives height 1-3 ft and width 1-2.5 ft (used here); UF/IFAS gives height 2 to 4 feet and spread 1 to 2 feet.

outdoor_sun_exposure omits full_shade: UF/IFAS prose says 'Salvia will perform well in full sun, partial shade, or full shade; however, flowering is reduced in partial shade.', but full shade is excluded by both structured sun fields (NC State Light lists only Full sun and Partial Shade; UF/IFAS's Light requirement reads 'plant grows in part shade/part sun'), so it is left out.
soil_base garden_bed is inferred from in-ground culture statements (sandy, fertile soil; clay with good drainage); no source gives a potting-mix recommendation.

is_houseplant is false: NC State's Landscape Location field lists Coastal, Naturalized Area and Walkways, it gives a USDA hardiness-zone range, and no admissible source frames this species as a houseplant. is_edible is null: no admissible source addresses it.

Temperature, humidity, light in foot-candles, fertilizing and chill damage: no admissible source states them. NC State lists USDA zones 8a-10b and UF/IFAS zones 7 through 11, but a hardiness zone is not a damage-onset temperature.

Tropical Sage and Blood Sage appear only in UF/IFAS's common-name list for this taxon. The UF/IFAS title leads with Scarlet Salvia, Scarlet Sage, so neither could be led by a page-title or first-item rule.

records.name_note: Sources split on the common name. NC State's Common Name(s) list for this species is alphabetized and reads Garden Coreopsis, Golden Coreopsis, Goldenwave, Plains Coreopsis, Tick-seed, the same five names in the same order as its page-title parenthetical. NC State's Description opens with "Plains coreopsis". RHS's dedicated page gives "dyer's tickseed" as its subtitle common name. Plains Coreopsis is used because it is the name NC State's Description opens with.
records.toxicity_detail: NC State's page for this species has no Poison block (no human-scoped severity rating). Its Tags list reads: "#bronze #maroon #drought tolerant #purple #full sun tolerant #clumping #medicinal #deer resistant #multistemmed #self-seeding #spreading #well-drained soil #pollinator plant #fall interest #NC native #sandy soils tolerant #rocky soils tolerant #native garden #butterfly friendly #pink flowers #non-toxic for cats #non-toxic for horses #non-toxic for dogs #dye plant #annual #tea #cpp #wildflower #poor soil tolerant #rain garden". The cat and dog scoping comes only from the #non-toxic for cats and #non-toxic for dogs tags. No other admissible source addressing toxicity was reachable.
unknowns: Missouri Botanical Garden's Plant Finder page for this taxon (taxonid=277179) could not be loaded in this session (TLS/connect errors), so no MoBot content is cited. No dedicated UF/IFAS, Clemson, PSU, UMD or UGA page was found.
is_houseplant is false: no admissible source addresses indoor culture; NC State (Plant Type Annual, Wildflower; Landscape Location Coastal, Naturalized Area) and RHS treat it as an outdoor annual.
soil_ph_min/max left null: NC State lists Acid (<6.0), Neutral (6.0-8.0) and Alkaline (>8.0) all as acceptable (open-ended bands) and RHS lists acid, alkaline or neutral.

water_regime left null: NC State's text says it 'should be watered lightly' and does not tolerate wet feet, but gives no explicit between-watering dry-down statement; its Soil Drainage field values are Good Drainage, Moist and Occasionally Dry. Not mapped to an enum value.

soil_drainage is moderate from NC State's Soil Drainage field values Good Drainage, Moist and Occasionally Dry; NC State prose also says it requires good drainage and does not tolerate 'wet feet', and RHS's Moisture field says Well–drained, so it sits at the drier end of moderate.

is_edible left null: NC State's ethnobotany note describes flowers boiled as a medicinal tea by Native Americans and carries a #tea tag, but no admissible source states the plant is grown or used for food.

RHS lists Name Status Correct and cites the common name 'dyer's tickseed'; RHS gives max height 0.5-1 m and spread 0.1-0.5 m, which differs from NC State's 24-48 in height and 12-18 in spread. NC State (dedicated page with Dimensions block) was used as the anchor.
No source gave a chill-damage temperature, temperature range, humidity, light in foot-candles, fertilizer schedule or watering interval; all left null.
NC State's outdoor Light field is Full sun (6 or more hours of direct sunlight a day); that is the legend-style category text so direct_sun_hours_max was not set from it.

records.name_note: Sources split on the lead common name. RHS's dedicated page for this species shows 'firewheel' as its common name and files 'Indian blanket' under 'Other common names'. NC State's page title carries an alphabetized parenthetical (Annual Gaillardia, Beach Blanket-flower, Bedding Gaillardia, Blanket Flower, Firewheel, Gaillardia, Indian Blanket Flower) and its description opens with 'Indian blanket flower'. The UF/IFAS page title is 'Blanket Flower, Gaillardia, Firewheel'. Firewheel is on all three lists; Indian Blanket (Flower) is on NC State's and RHS's.
unknowns: The Missouri Botanical Garden page for this species (plantfinder.mobot.org, kempercode=a578) refuses non-browser clients here, so it could not be read or quoted and nothing is cited from it.
toxic_to_pets and toxicity_detail are null: none of the NC State, RHS or UF/IFAS pages I read addresses toxicity to cats or dogs.
is_edible is null: no source addresses eating the plant. NC State's Ethnobotany field only mentions medicinal teas, which is not food use.

is_houseplant is false: no admissible source frames this as a houseplant. NC State says only that 'Indian blanket flower grows well in containers' (Landscape Location: Container), and UF/IFAS lists 'container or above-ground planter' among landscape uses.

water_regime is null: NC State says the plant needs soil that drains well and gets even moisture, tags it Occasionally Dry and lists drought tolerance, and UF/IFAS says not to over-water. No source gives a clear watering cadence, and drought tolerance alone cannot set the regime.

soil_drainage is set to fast from NC State (Good Drainage, Occasionally Dry, will not survive in water-logged soils) and UF/IFAS (light, very well-drained, sandy soil, root-rot warning). NC State prose also says 'even moisture', and constant moisture is advised only for germination.
soil_ph_min and soil_ph_max are null: NC State gives only the closed band Neutral (6.0-8.0), and RHS accepts acid, alkaline and neutral soils, so neither a floor nor a ceiling can be set.

direct_sun_hours_max is null: the only hour figures are NC State's generic light-category legend. RHS (Position Full sun) and UF/IFAS (Light requirement: plant grows in full sun) list full sun only. NC State's Light field also lists Partial Shade, and its prose says the plant 'tolerates light shade', but the UF/IFAS structured light field excludes shade, so part_shade was dropped and only full_sun is kept.

Mature spread differs by source: NC State gives 10-12 in (used, as the species' own structured Dimensions block), UF/IFAS gives 2 to 3 feet, and RHS gives 0.1-0.5 m. NC State height is 12-24 in, UF/IFAS 1 to 2 feet, and RHS 0.1-0.5 m.

NC State calls the species an 'erect annual or perennial' and lists Life Cycle Annual and Perennial. UF/IFAS's Plant type field lists annual; perennial; herbaceous, but its introduction calls them 'these annual flowers'. RHS tags it Annual Biennial and describes 'An upright, bushy annual to 45cm'. Perennial behaviour is therefore not firmly established.
Hardiness figures (NC State zones 5a-9b, UF/IFAS 3 through 11, RHS H4) are growing-range or survival ratings, not damage-onset temperatures, so chill_damage_f and the temperature fields are null.
No admissible source gives fertilizer, humidity, light in foot-candles, or watering-interval figures, so those fields are null.

records.name_note: The request name is "Nemesia", which is also the genus name. RHS's dedicated Nemesia strumosa page renders "Cape jewels" as its profile subtitle. NC State's page-title parenthetical reads "(Cape Jewels, Nemesia, Pouch Nemesia)" and its rendered Common Name(s) list, alphabetized in the same order, leads with Cape Jewels and also contains Nemesia and Pouch Nemesia. NC State's description prose opens with Pouch Nemesia; Cape Jewels is used because it leads both the RHS subtitle and NC State's list.
unknowns: Only NC State and RHS have dedicated N. strumosa pages among the admissible domains; no MoBot, UF/IFAS, Clemson, Penn State, UMD or UGA species page was found, and none was used.
toxic_to_pets, toxicity_detail and is_edible are null: neither admissible species page addresses toxicity or eating.
attracts_pollinators is null: neither page carries an attracts/pollinator field or statement.

soil_base is null: NC State gives texture (High Organic Matter, Loam (Silt), Sand) and says 'Soil requirements include well-drained, moist, loam, or sand with a neutral pH.'; its Landscape Location lists Container, Hanging Baskets and Houseplants and its prose names borders, flower beds, containers, or hanging baskets, so no single potting-mix or bed-soil base is stated.

soil_ph_min and soil_ph_max are null: NC State lists Neutral (6.0-8.0) while RHS lists pH as Acid or Neutral and its cultivation text says slightly acidic, so the NC State closed-band ceiling of 8.0 is not corroborated.

water_regime and all water/fertilizer fields are null: the only watering statement is RHS 'Water freely in dry weather to maintain flower production', which does not map cleanly to an enum value; 'Moist' is a soil-drainage tag, not a watering instruction. No fertilizer guidance on either page.

outdoor_sun_exposure part_sun comes from NC State's structured Light field 'Partial Shade (Direct sunlight only part of the day, 2-6 hours)', which this catalog maps to part_sun; RHS lists Full sun only. direct_sun_hours_max is null because the 6 or more and 2-6 hour figures are NC State's site-wide light-category legend, not species prose.

is_houseplant is true based on NC State listing Houseplants under Landscape Location and stating it may be grown as a short-lived houseplant; the plant is chiefly an annual for beds, borders and containers, with hardiness described by NC State as zones 2 to 10 (a hardiness rating, not a chill-damage temperature).
Temperature, humidity and light-intensity fields are null: the only temperature statement is the non-numeric 'They prefer cool to moderate temperatures'.
NC State notes that in hot climates it is best grown in spring or fall and that summer heat will result in die-back.
RHS Max Height and Max Spread (0.1-0.5 metres, about 3.9-19.7 inches) are not used for size; NC State's structured Dimensions block (6-12 in) is the anchor and its description prose agrees.

records.toxicity_detail: Source: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox page for Ipomoea x multifida. The page header says "This plant has low severity poison characteristics." The "Poisonous to Humans" block (human-scoped) reads: Poison Severity: Low; Poison Symptoms: Vomiting, large amounts of seeds may cause hallucinations; Poison Toxic Principle: Indole alkaloids (Lysergic acid, lysergamide, elymoclavine and chanoclavine); Causes Contact Dermatitis: No; Poison Part: Seeds. Separately from that human-scoped block, the page's Problems field lists Problem for Cats, Problem for Dogs and Problem for Horses, and its 14-tag Tags line carries the separate tags "#problem for dogs", "#problem for horses" and "#problem for cats"; no severity, symptom or plant-part detail is given for those animals. The page carries no handling, glove or sap warning. Plant Type on the page: Annual, Vine. The cat/dog Problems values are the sole basis for toxic_to_pets and come only from NC State.
unknowns: Only NC State has a page for this exact hybrid among the sources tried. RHS returned 404 for ipomoea-x-multifida and ipomoea-multifida; Clemson HGIC returned 403; plantfinder.mobot.org (refuses non-browser clients) and a Missouri Botanical Garden search URL could not be loaded. Nothing was borrowed from Ipomoea quamoclit or I. coccinea pages.

The synonym Ipomoea × sloteri is not stated on the NC State page; it is unverified from admissible sources, and scientific_name_accepted rests on NC State's own binomial (rendered with ASCII x, normalised to U+00D7) with no RHS Name Status check.

is_houseplant is false: the page describes an annual vine grown outdoors or in containers and hanging baskets (Landscape Location: Container, Vertical Spaces) and says nothing about indoor culture beyond starting seeds indoors.
toxic_to_pets=true rests only on NC State's Problem for Cats and Problem for Dogs entries; no symptoms or dose are given for pets, and the Poison block is human-scoped.

is_edible is null: no admissible source says the plant is grown for food; the page lists it as poisonous to humans (seeds, low severity) but does not address eating it, so no record is claimed either way.

NC State's Life Cycle field lists both Annual and Perennial, while Plant Type and the description say annual; hardiness zones 10a-12a are survival ratings, not a chill-damage onset, so chill_damage_f is null.

NC State's Light field legend text (full sun 6+ hours, partial shade 2-6 hours) is site-wide, so direct_sun_hours_max is null. Sun exposure comes from the Light field values; the description says full sun is preferred for best blooming.
soil_ph_max is null: the Neutral (6.0-8.0) band is NC State's only pH data and no RHS pH field was available to check a ceiling. soil_ph_min 6.0 is the floor of that band.
soil_base is null: the page gives soil texture and drainage but no potting-mix or garden-bed recommendation as such, and the plant is described for both ground and container use.
Watering, humidity, temperature, light in foot-candles and fertilizing are null: NC State's 'Moist' soil entry is a soil adjective, not a watering statement, and no admissible source gives the rest.

Size: the 'up to 10 feet tall and 1 foot wide' figure is a single maximum for a twining vine, so only the max ends are filled (10 ft = 120 in, 1 ft = 12 in); it may reflect length on a support rather than a self-supporting height. The page's separate 'Available Space To Plant: 3 feet-6 feet' field is a planting-space figure, not used.

records.name_note: NC State's Euphorbia marginata page has the bare binomial as its H1. Its alphabetized Common Name(s) list shows nine names, one per line (Ghost Weed, Mountain Snow, Mountain Spurge, Smoke-on-the-Prairie, Snow in Summer, Snow on the Mountain, Snow-on-the-mountain, Snow Thoroughwort, Variegated Spurge), and its page-title parenthetical gives the same nine names in the same order. The description opens with "Snow on the mountain". RHS's dedicated profile (plant 48585) renders snow on the mountain beneath its H1 and gives ghost weed, mountain snow, mountain spurge, snow in summer and snow thoroughwort as other common names. common_name uses the spelling Snow-on-the-Mountain, matching NC State's list entry 'Snow-on-the-mountain' apart from capitalization.
records.toxicity_detail: Sources: NC State Extension Plant Toolbox page for Euphorbia marginata, and RHS's dedicated profile (plant 48585). NC State's "Poisonous to Humans" block is human-scoped: Poison Severity: Low (page header: "This plant has low severity poison characteristics."). Poison Symptoms: "The milky white latex sap found in all plant parts can cause mild to severe contact dermatitis. If contact with the eyes occurs the sap can cause temporary to permanent damage to the cornea. If eaten, blistering can occur on lips and oral mucosa. Avoid ingesting plant parts and keep plants away from pets and children." Poison Toxic Principle: Diterpene esters in milky latex. Causes Contact Dermatitis: Yes. Poison Part: Bark, Flowers, Fruits, Leaves, Roots, Seeds, Stems. Handling warning from the description: "Stems and leaves contain a milky latex sap that can cause contact dermatitis for some. Be sure to wear protective gloves. Keep this plant out of the reach of children and pets. It is toxic if ingested." The general 'pets and children' advice names no specific animal. NC State's Problems list carries Contact Dermatitis, Poisonous to Humans, Problem for Cats, Problem for Children, Problem for Dogs and Weedy. Its Tags line carries #contact dermatitis, #problem for children, #problem for dogs, #poisonous, #problem for cats and #poisonous if ingested. The cat and dog tags carry no severity rating or symptom list of their own. Plant Type values: Annual, Poisonous, Wildflower. RHS's Potentially harmful field reads "Humans/Pets: IRRITANT to skin/eye; harmful if eaten." and "Wear gloves and other protective equipment when handling." It names pets without naming cats or dogs. The two sources agree. Handle with gloves and keep away from eyes.
unknowns: NC State and RHS's dedicated profile (plant 48585) are the admissible pages reached. MoBot (www.missouribotanicalgarden.org and plantfinder.mobot.org) returned connection errors, Clemson HGIC returned 403, and no dedicated UF/IFAS or UMD page was found. RHS agrees with NC State on name, sun (Full sun, Partial shade), well-drained soil, pH (Acid or Alkaline or Neutral) and harm. Its Max Spread of 0.1-0.5 metres is narrower than NC State's 1-2 ft width. NC State's figure is landed.

scientific_name_accepted is cited to NC State's page heading. RHS's dedicated profile has the H1 Euphorbia marginata, but its Name Status field reads Unresolved, not Correct, so no RHS confirmation of accepted status exists.
is_houseplant is false: NC State frames it as an annual for naturalized areas and borders (Landscape Location: Meadow, Naturalized Area, Slope/Bank) and states nothing about indoor culture.

toxic_to_pets=true rests on NC State's separate Problem for Cats and Problem for Dogs tags; the 'keep away from pets and children' sentence names no animal and is kept unscoped. NC State's Poison block (severity Low) is human-scoped. No cat/dog symptom list or severity exists on the page.
is_edible=false rests on NC State's 'It is toxic if ingested.' and 'Avoid ingesting plant parts'; no source mentions any edible use.

soil_drainage left null: NC State lists Good Drainage + Occasionally Dry (no wet tag) but also Clay among the Soil Texture values and the prose says only 'well-drained', so fast vs moderate is not settled by the source.
soil pH left null: NC State lists Acid (<6.0), Neutral (6.0-8.0) and Alkaline (>8.0), whose open-ended bands give no floor or ceiling.
water_regime and fertilizer fields left null: NC State states drought tolerance and 'Dry Soil' resistance as traits but gives no watering or feeding instruction.

direct_sun_hours_max left null: the only hour figures on the page are in the site-wide light legend. The species prose says only 'They prefer full sun' and that in hot summer climates some protection from hot afternoon sun may be needed.
outdoor_sun_exposure: full_sun from the Light field's full-sun tag and part_shade from the Partial Shade tag. The prose adds that too much shade makes plants floppy.
Species is an annual (NC State Life Cycle: Annual) that reseeds and is tagged Weedy; this matters for garden placement.

The NC State alias 'Snow in Summer' is also used for Cerastium tomentosum, a separate landed species, and Euphorbia hypericifolia ('Diamond Frost') is a separate sibling; neither is merged here. No citation to those other species' pages was gathered.
Temperature, humidity, light footcandle, chill damage and fertilizer values are null because no admissible source reached states them.

records.name_note: Sources lead with different names. RHS's page for the hybrid is headed Pericallis × hybrida with 'florist's cineraria' as its common-name subtitle. NC State's page-title parenthetical lists three names, Cineraria, Common Ragwort and Florist's Cineraria, and its Common Name(s) list leads with Cineraria. Florist's Cineraria was chosen because the hybrid's own RHS page leads with it and NC State lists it too; NC State's 'Common Ragwort' alias was ignored. NC State gives Cineraria x hybrida as a previous name and RHS lists Cineraria × hybrida as a synonym. NC State's description prose also opens with 'Florists’ cineraria'.
unknowns: Toxicity: neither the NC State nor the RHS page for this hybrid says anything about toxicity to cats, dogs or people, so toxic_to_pets and toxicity_detail are null. Nothing was inferred from Senecio pyrrolizidine data.

Missouri Botanical Garden's page for the hybrid (plantfinder.mobot.org, kempercode=b563) could not be loaded: the www.missouribotanicalgarden.org URL redirects to plantfinder.mobot.org, which failed here with a connection or certificate error. MoBot content is therefore not used. This is why humidity, temperature, edibility, pollinator and other fields are null. The page should be retried later.
No UF/IFAS, Clemson, PSU, UMD or UGA page dedicated to Pericallis × hybrida turned up in a search, so none is used. The UF/IFAS hit was for Senecio cineraria (dusty miller), a different plant.

outdoor_sun_exposure: NC State's structured Light field and its prose say partial shade only. RHS's structured Position field lists 'Full sun, Partial shade', but RHS is UK-calibrated and NC State is the only other source, so full_sun is left out. RHS's Position is full sun and partial shade, which disagrees with NC State here.
direct_sun_hours_max is null. The only hours figure on the NC State page is the generic '2-6 hours' text inside its Light legend for the Partial Shade category, not species-specific prose.

water_regime is null. NC State's only moisture wording is the soil adjective 'fertile, well-drained and constantly moist soil', which this catalog does not read as a watering cadence. RHS Moisture reads 'Moist but well–drained or Well–drained', and RHS's genus-style Cultivation line says only 'Keep watered, especially during dry periods'. No watering interval or dry-down target is stated.

soil_drainage is moderate. NC State's structured Soil Drainage pair is Good Drainage and Moist, and its prose says 'well-drained and constantly moist soil'. RHS Moisture reads 'Moist but well–drained or Well–drained'.
soil_ph: RHS lists Acid or Alkaline or Neutral, which gives no bound. NC State gives no pH. Both ends are null.
soil_base is null. The sources say 'fertile' soil and NC State's Soil Texture is High Organic Matter, but neither names a potting-mix type.
chill_damage_f is null. RHS's H1C is a UK hardiness rating (minimum 5 to 10 C for growing outside in summer), and NC State's zones 9a-11b are a hardiness range. Neither is a damage-onset temperature.

Size: mature_height_in 12-18 and mature_spread_in 12-24 come from NC State's description prose ('12 to 18 inches high and 1 to 2 feet wide'). NC State's structured Dimensions block reads 'Height: 1 ft. 6 in. - 1 ft. 0 in.', which is inverted or malformed, and 'Width: 1 ft. 0 in. - 2 ft. 0 in.'. RHS's Max Height and Max Spread are both 0.5-1 metres (19.7-39.4 in), which is larger and was not used.

NC State's Life Cycle values are Annual and Perennial, and its Plant Type values are Annual and Herbaceous Perennial. RHS's plant-type tags are Herbaceous Perennial, Annual Biennial and Houseplants. The plant is treated as an annual or houseplant in North Carolina.

RHS's Cultivation paragraph is genus-style boilerplate for Pericallis, so it was not used for any field except the 'Keep watered' counterpoint. Fertilizer, humidity, temperature and light-intensity guidance are absent from both usable pages.
Edibility and pollinator attraction are not addressed by NC State or RHS for this hybrid, so is_edible and attracts_pollinators are null.

water_regime, water_dry_down_target and the day-interval fields left null: no source gives a watering statement. NC State only says it will not tolerate wet feet and tags it drought tolerant (a tolerance trait); RHS gives a structured moisture field of 'Moist but well–drained or Well–drained'.

soil_drainage set moderate on RHS's structured Moisture field 'Moist but well–drained or Well–drained'; NC State's Soil Drainage field is the bare 'Good Drainage' (not fast; the page also warns of root rot without good drainage). UF/IFAS gives no drainage statement. RHS's Cultivation sentence 'Grow in full sun, in any moist but free-draining soil, as long as it isn't too acidic' is not used: the identical sentence is the Cultivation text of RHS's Scabiosa columbaria 'Mariposa Blue' profile, so it is stock text rather than species-specific culture.

soil_ph_min 6.0 is the floor of NC State's closed Neutral (6.0-8.0) band, consistent with RHS's structured pH field "Alkaline or Neutral"; soil_ph_max null because NC State's Alkaline (>8.0) band is open-ended; UF/IFAS lists acidic among soil tolerances, which conflicts.

UF/IFAS describes this as a 12-inch-tall herbaceous perennial in its intro while its Plant type is annual and its height is 1 to 3 feet; NC State and RHS call it an annual. UF/IFAS height 1-3 ft and spread 1-2 ft and RHS Max Height 0.5-1 m, Max Spread 0.5-1 m differ from NC State's width (9-12 in); NC State's Dimensions block was used as the anchor.
No MoBot page for the species itself was located (only cultivar pages such as Beaujolais Bonnets), so none is cited.

Temperature, humidity, light-in-footcandles, fertilizer and chill-damage fields have no admissible species-specific figures and are null. NC State zone range 4a-11b is a hardiness listing, not a damage onset. Some floras place this species as Sixalix atropurpurea; no admissible source was checked for that name.

normalizations: 2026-10-09: b119 (annuals, bedding and container plants) landed from the post-audit records. Eight species: Bloody Sage, Plains Coreopsis, Firewheel, Cape Jewels, Cardinal Climber, Snow-on-the-Mountain, Florist's Cineraria, Pincushion Flower. Auditor-supplied corrected wording used verbatim; every substitute quote ground-truthed with qc.py and a strict consecutive-node check (b119_qcheck.py) before it was applied. Landing decisions: the two hybrids keep U+00D7 in both name fields (Ipomoea × multifida, Pericallis × hybrida); Firewheel's outdoor_sun_exposure cut to full_sun (UF/IFAS Light requirement and RHS Position full sun only; NC State's Partial Shade and 'tolerates light shade' aside dropped); Florist's Cineraria's water_regime stays null (NC State's 'constantly moist soil' is a soil adjective) and its water citation is dropped; Bloody Sage's mislabelled soil_drainage citation split into a UF/IFAS citation and an NC State 'Good Drainage' citation, and its full_shade unknowns entry corrected to UF/IFAS's partial-shade hedge; space-joined NC State tag runs ('#non-toxic for cats #non-toxic for horses #non-toxic for dogs', '#problem for dogs #problem for horses #problem for cats') split into separate single-tag quotes, and Snow-on-the-Mountain's truncated tag-line slice replaced by its stacked Problems field; Cardinal Climber's label-only 'Causes Contact Dermatitis:' quote and three single-field poison quotes replaced by the page's contiguous Poison block, and Snow-on-the-Mountain gains its contiguous Poison block, RHS's Potentially harmful field and RHS name citations (RHS Name Status there reads Unresolved); every <title>-only NC State parenthetical (and RHS's pipe-joined <title>) replaced by the rendered Common Name(s) list, rendered H1 or rendered subtitle; bare RHS 'Correct' kept only in the CORR form beside a rendered H1 naming the taxon; label+value quotes cut to the value (UF/IFAS Common name(s), Light requirement; RHS Name Status); Pincushion Flower's RHS stock Cultivation sentence replaced by RHS's structured Moisture and pH fields; is_houseplant set false (NC State Landscape Location / hardiness-zone / Plant Type citations) for the six landscape species where it was null; RHS moisture strings quoted in unknowns given the page's en dashes. toxic_to_pets true for Cardinal Climber (NC State Problems: Problem for Cats/Dogs) and Snow-on-the-Mountain (NC State Problems: Problem for Cats/Dogs; RHS's 'Humans/Pets' line names no animal); false for Bloody Sage and Plains Coreopsis (NC State's separate #non-toxic for cats / #non-toxic for dogs tags); the rest null. No common name collided with a landed species (Scarlet Sage, NC State's prose name for Salvia coccinea, is Salvia splendens's landed name, disclosed in Bloody Sage's name_note).
